title: Hoops lifting out of pressed pigment

tokens.v: A shallow pan of loose ultramarine pigment has been pressed flat and then cracked, a fine craquelure running across the packed surface with one plate tipped and crumbling back into fresh powder. Both hoops sat half-sunk in that bed; one has just been lifted clear on the tip of a fine steel tweezer and trails a hanging veil of pigment dust that has not yet fallen, individual grains resolving where the light catches them, a soft blue collar left in the pan where it was seated. 100mm macro at f/4, framed 1:1 life-size, just above bed level, one hard raking key from the right so every crack wall takes a bright line and the dust lights against unfilled shadow - deep ultramarine against warm polished gold and nothing else in the palette; the lifted hoop stands about a third of the frame across. The VERITY STONE punch on the hinge post reads as a single struck dot, unlettered at this scale, taking one point of the key. Loose pigment blurs across the bottom edge, cut by both corners.
